claims.text: Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 is initially in a high-temperature BCC state.
Cooling and subsequent thermal exposure govern phase evolution in Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7.
The relevant thermal-exposure range is 500–800 °C under vacuum annealing.
The phase stability of Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 is governed by competition between BCC and FCC or HCP phase formation.
Valence electron concentration influences whether HCP, BCC, or FCC phases form.
Atomic-size difference influences phase stability in Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7.
VEC and atomic-size difference act as the structural mediator during cooling and annealing.
Depending on VEC and atomic-size difference, the target alloy will form either a single BCC phase or a phase mixture.
Ti31Zr33Hf36 film provides a single-HCP-phase baseline.
A VEC interval of approximately 4.09–6.87 defines the proposed applicability boundary.
An atomic-size difference below 15% defines the proposed applicability boundary.
GIXRD can identify phases and provide lattice constants after annealing.
The hypothesis would be falsified if phase stability were not influenced by VEC or atomic-size difference.

contradictions.description: The nominal composition—and therefore its composition-derived VEC and atomic-size difference—is fixed for Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 during cooling or annealing, while the experiment proposes varying VEC and atomic-size difference. Doing so requires changing composition, so it would no longer be a comparison solely within the stated alloy.

The stated Ti31Zr33Hf36 baseline is a chemically unrelated HCP alloy, whereas the proposed experiment does not specify using it or define a matched Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 control. Thus the baseline is not operationally connected to the controlled comparison.
